newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish telecms, IT firms see big net sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Finnish telecms, IT firms see big net sales growth.

text.p: Finnish telecoms and information technology (IT) companies expect their net sales to increase significantly in the next few years, state-owned financing company Start Fund of Kera Oy said on Wednesday.

"By the year 2000, annual turnover will amount to about 125 billion markka," Kera said in a statement, referring to a survey of 120 Finnish telecoms and IT companies. In 1996, these companies' combined net sales were about 55 billion markka.
The figures include Finland's telecoms flagship Nokia Oy, Kera said, noting that excluding Nokia, last year's turnover of the companies surveyed was 17 billion markka.

"Finnish IT companies believe that their products are very strong and competitive," Kera said. The survey found that the companies saw technological know-how and product development as their strong sides while exports and marketing were weaker areas.
In 1996, the telecoms and IT cluster employed 52,000 people. By 2000, the companies surveyed -- excluding Nokia -- expected to create some 4,000 new jobs, Kera said.
Some companies expected the lack of skilled workers to hold back growth, it added.

"Nearly all companies expected to be able to finance growth out of cash flow," Kera said. If not, companies said they were likely to turn to specialised financiers or venture capital companies for assistance.
